Events & the WebSocket Stream ​

Two different things in Saidi are called "events", and they do not touch each other:

  • WebSocket frames — what the orchestrator pushes to open dashboards so a run or chat renders live.
  • Bus events — the normalized envelope every producer funnels into emitEvent(), which reflexes match on.

This page documents both, plus the durable RunEvent that sits between them.

The endpoint ​

The WebSocket server is attached to the same HTTP server as the API, at path /ws — so the client connects to wss://<your-workspace-host>/ws.

PropertyValue
Path/ws
Max frame payload256 KiB
Origin checkCloud only; the handshake is refused unless Origin's host matches Host or SAIDI_PUBLIC_URL. A missing Origin falls through to session auth
Auth (local)None. Everything is the single local org
Auth (cloud)The saidi_session cookie rides the same-origin upgrade, plus a ?org=<orgId> query parameter
wss://<your-workspace-host>/ws            # same origin as the app
wss://your-host/ws?org=<orgId>            # cloud — cookie carries the session

In cloud mode the socket authenticates before any frame is served: the session is validated, the ?org= value is membership-checked, the org must be active, and the socket is then tagged with { orgId, userId, runsViewAll, chatsViewAll }. A platform superadmin may open any workspace with owner-level visibility.

Close codes ​

CodeMeaning
1013MongoDB is unavailable — the socket refuses to serve or accept frames
4401Unauthenticated, or the session was revoked (logout, password reset). The client should stop reconnecting and log out
4403Membership changed or the org was suspended. The client reconnects and re-authenticates with fresh governance

Sockets cache session, org, role, and permissions at handshake time, so the only way to revoke access is to close them — which is what closeOrgUserSockets / closeUserSocketsEverywhere / closeOrgSockets do.

Connecting ​

On a successful connection the server sends one ready frame, then replays snapshot frames so a refreshed tab rejoins any process-global turns already running without restarting the work:

json
{ "type": "ready", "projects": 7 }
{ "type": "turn_start",      "id": "…", "conversationId": "…" }
{ "type": "message_state",   "id": "…", "state": "running", "conversationId": "…" }
{ "type": "stream_snapshot", "id": "…", "eventId": "…", "text": "…so far", "conversationId": "…" }
{ "type": "queue",           "n": 2, "conversationId": "…" }

Two independent liveness mechanisms run:

  • Protocol heartbeat. The server pings every socket every 30 s and terminates any client that did not answer the previous ping. Terminating fires the connection's close handler, which deliberately does not abort an in-flight text turn — those are process-global and survive a dropped tab.
  • App-level keepalive. The client may send { "type": "ping" } and time the { "type": "pong" } reply, which detects a half-open TCP socket that the protocol ping cannot.

Each socket is rate-limited to 60 frames per second in a fixed 1 s window; anything past the cap is dropped silently. A socket may also target at most 32 distinct chats over its lifetime.

Frames the client sends ​

typeFieldsEffect
ping—Answered with pong, nothing else
usertext, id?, conversationId?, attachments?, mode?Enqueue a main-chat turn. mode: 'voice' marks it as a voice turn
cancelidCancel the named turn (queued or active)
resetconversationId?/clear — flush the queue, drop the session, erase that chat's durable activity
confirm_responseid, approvedAnswer a confirm card
realtime_transcriptturnId, role (user | assistant), textRecord a voice turn's transcript; an assistant role releases the turn
realtime_tool_callturnId, callId, name, arguments?Execute one PRIME tool for the voice session; answered with realtime_tool_result
realtime_cancelturnIdAbort the voice turn and release its liveness

attachments entries are { file, alt? } and are only accepted if the file already exists in the chat uploads directory (upload it over HTTP first). At most 12 per message.

A conversationId you may not access is dropped, never silently rewritten to another chat — the server replies with an error frame instead. Only the literal placeholder 'main' maps to your own default chat.

Two frames are not chat-specific:

typePayloadMeaning
agent_stateactor, state (idle | active | thinking)Lights or clears a node in the orchestration graph

wallet—The wallet moved. Deliberately amount-free, so each dashboard re-fetches a balance scoped to its own viewer

Frames the server sends — runs ​

typePayloadMeaning
run_updaterun (a RunSummary)Durable state changed — status, participants, branch — or a live lastActivity progress line
run_eventrunId, event (a RunEvent)A new committed thread entry
run_deltarunId, streamId, actor, text, seqA streaming token chunk for the live segment
run_segment_endrunId, streamIdThe live segment closed; its final text arrives as a run_event
run_truncatedrunId, fromEventIdA rewind — drop this event and everything after it
run_removedrunIdThe run was permanently deleted

Every thread entry — messages, worker text blocks, tool rows, results — goes through runs.appendEvent, which persists it and broadcasts it exactly once via the store's single observer. There is no separate "ephemeral thread event" path, so live and saved can never diverge. Only run_delta and the live activity line are ephemeral by design.

run_delta carries a per-stream seq counter, incremented per frame and reset when the segment ends. A frame delivered twice (a ghost socket in a long-lived tab, a reconnect overlap) repeats its seq, so clients drop it instead of garbling the live text.

How a client subscribes to a run ​

There is no subscribe frame. Subscription is implicit and enforced server-side:

  1. Open /ws (with ?org= in cloud mode).
  2. Fetch the run over HTTP — GET /api/runs/:id returns the full thread.
  3. Apply every subsequent frame whose runId matches; ignore the rest.

The server decides what reaches you. Content-bearing run frames go only to sockets that may view the run: the creator's, anyone in run.sharedWith, and any member holding runs.viewAll in that org. Everything else is filtered out before the send, so a member never receives another member's un-shared run stream — including live token deltas, which mirror the committed-event path exactly.

Main-chat frames use the same mechanism with chats.viewAll.

The bus event envelope ​

Every producer — the run engine, webhook ingress, pollers, agents — reduces its raw payload to one normalized Event and hands it to emitEvent(). This is the shape reflex rules match against.

ts
interface Event {
  id: string;                          // unique — used for dedup / idempotency
  at: number;                          // epoch ms
  source: string;                      // event family
  type: string;                        // event type within the source
  actor?: string;                      // who/what triggered it
  payload: Record<string, unknown>;    // normalized, matchable fields
  raw?: unknown;                       // the untouched original, for audit / re-parse
  runId?: string;                      // set when it originated inside a run
  depth?: number;                      // chain depth; the bus loop-guard caps it
  orgId?: string;                      // owning org — matching is same-org scoped
}

Real source values ​

sourceProducer
runThe run-lifecycle producer (reflexes/engine.ts)
agentAn agent or PRIME calling the raise_event tool. Always emitted at depth: 1
genericPOST /api/webhooks/generic
githubPOST /api/webhooks/github
stripePOST /api/webhooks/stripe
whatsapp, instagram, messengerMeta ingress, resolved from the payload or the URL you posted to
any nameThe env-configured webhook path — POST /api/webhooks/<name> with SAIDI_WEBHOOK_<NAME>_* set
operator-chosenA reflex whose action is emitEvent sets its own source, at depth + 1

Real run types ​

typeEmitted when
run.finishedThe run reached done
run.failedThe run reached error
run.needs_approvalThe run is awaiting_input and holds a pending approval gate
run.cost_exceededThe run's cumulative cost crossed runCostAlertUsd. Fires once per run

Payload for the first three: { runId, title, status, message }. For run.cost_exceeded: { runId, title, costUsd, threshold }. All four carry actor = the run title and runId = the run.

Paused, cancelled, and plain awaiting_input transitions emit nothing.

Naming for webhook types follows the source: GitHub becomes <x-github-event>.<action> (e.g. pull_request.opened), Stripe passes its own type through (e.g. payment_intent.succeeded), and Meta flattens to whatsapp.text, whatsapp.status.delivered, messenger.postback, and so on.

What the bus does with an event ​

emitEvent() is the single seam, and the one place safety lives:

GuardBehaviour
DedupThe orgId:eventId pair is remembered (2000 ids). A repeat is dropped — retried webhooks and overlapping pollers are free
Loop guarddepth > 3 is dropped and logged
Rate limit120 events per source per 60 s window, keyed per org, so one tenant's flood cannot throttle another's
Per-reflexMax-fires cap, cooldown, dedup key, and the approval gate, in that order

Dedup and rate-limit keys are always org-prefixed; a single workspace collapses to the single local key. Every event that reaches the matcher is logged with how many reflexes matched it, which is what feeds the reflex_event frame.

A matched reflex reserves its fire slot synchronously — fireCount++, lastFiredAt, auto-disable at the cap — before its async action dispatches, so a burst arriving in one tick cannot read stale counters and blow past maxFires. If the action then fails, the reservation is rolled back so a failure does not consume the cap.

Raising an event by hand ​

Any agent (PRIME included) can put an event on the bus with the raise_event tool — see Orchestrator Tools. It is fixed to source: 'agent' and depth: 1, so it is loop-guarded like anything else. The HTTP equivalent for external systems is the webhook ingress.
